title: CCS (Implementation of National Pension System) Rules, 2021 & Latest Official Updates (Up to 2026) — Exhaustive Exam-Oriented Flashcards

cards.front: [Enacting Formula / Preamble | Constitutional Basis] Under which exact articles/clauses of the Constitution of India were the CCS (Implementation of National Pension System) Rules, 2021 framed, and whose consultation was mandatory?
cards.back:
**Constitutional Powers:** Framed by the **President** in exercise of powers conferred by:
1. **Proviso to Article 309** of the Constitution, AND
2. **Clause (5) of Article 148** of the Constitution.

**Mandatory Consultation:** Framed after consultation with the **Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (C&AG)** in relation to persons serving in the **Indian Audit and Accounts Department (IA&AD)**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Do NOT mark 'Article 309 only' or 'PFRDA Act, 2013' as the rule-making power. Both Proviso to Art. 309 AND Art. 148(5) (with C&AG consultation for IA&AD) are invoked.
cards.exam_trap: Do NOT mark 'Article 309 only' or 'PFRDA Act, 2013' as the rule-making power. Both Proviso to Art. 309 AND Art. 148(5) (with C&AG consultation for IA&AD) are invoked.

cards.front: [Notification Header & Rule 1(1)–(2) | Timeline / Deadline] What is the official Gazette Notification number, nodal Department, signing date, and exact commencement date of the CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021?
cards.back:
- **Short Title [Rule 1(1)]:** *Central Civil Services (Implementation of National Pension System) Rules, 2021*.
- **Nodal Ministry/Dept:** Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions (**Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare — DoPPW**).
- **Notification No.:** **G.S.R. 227(E)**, Extraordinary Gazette Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (i).
- **Date on Notification:** **30th March, 2021**.
- **Commencement [Rule 1(2)]:** Came into force on the **date of publication in the Official Gazette** (**31st March, 2021**, as cited in DoPPW O.M. dated 14.10.2024 & CPAO Official Compendium).

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Rule 1(2) does NOT give retrospective effect from 01.01.2004 — the Rules came into force prospectively on Official Gazette publication (30/31.03.2021), though they apply to employees appointed on or after 01.01.2004.
cards.exam_trap: Rule 1(2) does NOT give retrospective effect from 01.01.2004 — the Rules came into force prospectively on Official Gazette publication (30/31.03.2021), though they apply to employees appointed on or after 01.01.2004.

cards.front: [Rule 2 (Opening Clause) | Sub-rule / Clause] To which class of Government servants do the CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021 apply under the opening part of Rule 2?
cards.back:
Save as otherwise provided in these rules, they apply to:
- **Government servants**, INCLUDING **civilian Government servants in the Defence Services**,
- Appointed **substantively** to civil services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union,
- **On or after the 1st day of January, 2004**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Notice TWO key phrases: (1) 'including civilian Government servants in the Defence Services' ARE covered (armed forces personnel under Army/Navy/Air Force Acts are NOT); (2) 'on or after 01.01.2004' (whereas Armed Forces other than civilians remained under OPS even after 01.01.2004).
cards.exam_trap: Notice TWO key phrases: (1) 'including civilian Government servants in the Defence Services' ARE covered (armed forces personnel under Army/Navy/Air Force Acts are NOT); (2) 'on or after 01.01.2004' (whereas Armed Forces other than civilians remained under OPS even after 01.01.2004).

cards.front: [Rule 2(a) to 2(h) | Exception] List ALL EIGHT statutory categories of persons explicitly EXCLUDED from the CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021 under clauses (a) to (h) of Rule 2.
cards.exam_trap: Probationers appointed substantively against regular posts ARE covered (see Rule 6(6)), whereas contract, casual, daily-rated, contingency-paid, Railway, and AIS officers are excluded under Rule 2(a)–(h).

cards.front: [Rule 2(h) + DoPPW OMs (03.03.2023, 20.10.2023 & 22.06.2026) | 2024–2026 Update] Which employees appointed on or after 01.01.2004 are excluded under Rule 2(h) because CCS (Pension) Rules apply to them by special/general Government orders (latest up to 2026)?
cards.back:
1. **Pre-22.12.2003 Vacancy/Notification Cases (DoPPW OM No. 57/05/2021-P&PW(B) dt. 03.03.2023):** Central Govt civil employees appointed against posts/vacancies **advertised/notified for recruitment/appointment on or before 22.12.2003** (date of NPS notification) were given a **one-time option up to 31.08.2023** (orders to be issued by 30.11.2023) to be covered under CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972 (now 2021).
2. **Technical Resignation / Mobility Cases (DoPPW OM dt. 20.10.2023):** Employees who joined pre-01.01.2004 (or were covered under OPS via OM dt. 03.03.2023) in Central/State Govt or Autonomous Body and moved to Central Govt with proper permission/technical resignation.
3. **Compassionate Appointments (DoPPW OM dt. 22.06.2026):** Crucial date clarification governing eligibility for OPS coverage in compassionate appointment cases.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Crucial cut-off date in OM dt. 03.03.2023 is 22.12.2003 (date of MoF NPS Notification), NOT 31.12.2003! Earlier OM dt. 17.02.2020 required result declaration before 01.01.2004; OM dt. 03.03.2023 relaxed it to advertisement/notification on or before 22.12.2003.
cards.exam_trap: Crucial cut-off date in OM dt. 03.03.2023 is 22.12.2003 (date of MoF NPS Notification), NOT 31.12.2003! Earlier OM dt. 17.02.2020 required result declaration before 01.01.2004; OM dt. 03.03.2023 relaxed it to advertisement/notification on or before 22.12.2003.

cards.front: [Rule 2 + DoPPW OM dt. 25.10.2024 & MoF/CSIR 2026 | 2024–2026 Update] Do the CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021 (and Rule 10 OPS death/disability options) apply automatically to employees of Central Autonomous Bodies (CABs)?
cards.back:
**NO.**
- Vide **DoPPW O.M. No. 57/03/2022-P&PW(B)/8361(8) dated 25.10.2024**, DoPPW clarified that service matters of Autonomous Body employees do **not** fall under DoPPW's jurisdiction; hence CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021 and OM dt. 26.10.2022 are **NOT suo-moto applicable** to employees of Autonomous Bodies.
- Reaffirmed by **Ministry of Finance (Dept. of Expenditure) ID Note dt. 23.02.2026** (communicated e.g. in CSIR OM dt. 24.03.2026), denying automatic extension of Rule 10 OPS benefits to CAB employees.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Frequent assertion-reason question: CAB employees may be subscribed to NPS, yet CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021 apply ONLY to Central Govt civil employees unless specifically extended with MoF concurrence.
cards.exam_trap: Frequent assertion-reason question: CAB employees may be subscribed to NPS, yet CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021 apply ONLY to Central Govt civil employees unless specifically extended with MoF concurrence.

cards.front: [Rule 2 read with CCS (Implementation of UPS under NPS) Rules, 2025 | 2024–2026 Update] How does the notification of the CCS (Implementation of the Unified Pension Scheme under NPS) Rules, 2025 [G.S.R. 599(E) dt. 02.09.2025] affect applicability of the 2021 CCS NPS Rules?
cards.back:
- **UPS Effective Date:** **01.04.2025** (MoF Notification dt. 24.01.2025; PFRDA Regulations dt. 19.03.2025; DoPPW UPS Rules notified **02.09.2025**).
- Central Govt NPS employees who **opt for UPS** are governed by the **CCS (Implementation of the UPS under NPS) Rules, 2025**.
- Under **Rule 2(i)** of the 2025 UPS Rules, employees to whom CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021 apply and who **have NOT opted for UPS** continue under the 2021 CCS NPS Rules.
- UPS optees also get a **one-time switch facility back to NPS** (exercisable up to **1 year before superannuation** or **3 months before VRS**), upon which they revert to NPS rules.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: UPS is notified as an 'option under NPS', NOT a repeal of CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021.
cards.rule_ref: Rule 2 read with CCS (Implementation of UPS under NPS) Rules, 2025
cards.exam_trap: UPS is notified as an 'option under NPS', NOT a repeal of CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021.

cards.front: [Rule 2(b) & 2(h) + DoPPW OMs (26.02.2016 / 28.07.2016) | Exception] What is the statutory exception under Rule 2(b) & Rule 2(h) for Casual Labourers granted 'Temporary Status' before 01.01.2004 (under the DoPT 1993 Scheme) who are regularised in Group 'C' ON OR AFTER 01.01.2004?
cards.back:
- **General Exclusion [Rule 2(b)]:** Persons in *casual and daily rated employment* are excluded from CCS (NPS) Rules, 2021.
- **Pre-2004 Temporary Status Exception [Rule 2(h) + DoPPW OMs dt. 26.02.2016 & 28.07.2016]:** Casual labourers who had been conferred **Temporary Status under the 'Casual Labourers (Grant of Temporary Status and Regularisation) Scheme of Government of India, 1993' on or before 31.12.2003**, and were subsequently **regularised on or after 01.01.2004**, are **EXEMPTED from NPS** and governed by **CCS (Pension) Rules (OPS)** *(with **50%** of Temporary Status service counting towards qualifying service)*!
- **Contrast:** Casual workers engaged *without* pre-01.01.2004 1993-Scheme Temporary Status who are appointed substantively on or after 01.01.2004 ARE covered by CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: High-yield Rule 2(b) vs 2(h) exception: Pre-01.01.2004 Temporary Status Casual Labourers (1993 Scheme) regularised even in 2010/2020 get OPS (with 50% temporary-status service credit), NOT NPS!
cards.exam_trap: High-yield Rule 2(b) vs 2(h) exception: Pre-01.01.2004 Temporary Status Casual Labourers (1993 Scheme) regularised even in 2010/2020 get OPS (with 50% temporary-status service credit), NOT NPS!

cards.front: [Rule 2 + DoPPW OM 25.10.2024 vs EPFO (Staff & Conditions of Service) Regulations, 2025 | Exception] Explain the two-sided legal rule on Autonomous / Statutory Bodies: Why are Central Autonomous Bodies excluded suo-moto [OM dt. 25.10.2024], yet how were CCS (NPS) Rules, 2021 applied to EPFO employees in May 2025 — and with what UPSC exception?
cards.back:
1. **No Automatic (`Suo-Moto`) Application [DoPPW OM dt. 25.10.2024 & MoF Note dt. 23.02.2026]:** CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021 are framed under **Art. 309** for Union civil servants and **do NOT apply automatically** to Autonomous/Statutory Bodies.
2. **Express Statutory Adoption Example — `EPFO (Staff and Conditions of Service) Regulations, 2025` (Notified May 2025):**
   - Explicitly adopted **CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021** and **CCS (Payment of Gratuity under NPS) Rules, 2021** for regular employees of the Central Board (EPFO) appointed on or after 01.01.2004.
   - **Express Proviso / Exception:** Consultation with **UPSC** (required for Central Govt retirees under the 1st Proviso to Rule 5(1) of CCS Gratuity under NPS Rules before withholding/withdrawing gratuity) **SHALL NOT BE APPLICABLE** to Central Board employees!

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Sharp distinction for UPSC / EPFO / SAS exams: Autonomous bodies never get CCS NPS Rules suo-moto; they apply ONLY where expressly adopted by statutory regulation/MoF approval (with body-specific modifications such as excluding UPSC consultation)!
cards.rule_ref: Rule 2 + DoPPW OM 25.10.2024 vs EPFO (Staff & Conditions of Service) Regulations, 2025
cards.exam_trap: Sharp distinction for UPSC / EPFO / SAS exams: Autonomous bodies never get CCS NPS Rules suo-moto; they apply ONLY where expressly adopted by statutory regulation/MoF approval (with body-specific modifications such as excluding UPSC consultation)!

cards.front: [Rule 3(1)(a) & 3(1)(v) | Sub-rule / Clause] Distinguish between 'Accredited Bank' [Rule 3(1)(a)] and 'Trustee Bank' [Rule 3(1)(v)] under the CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021.
cards.back:
- **Accredited Bank [Rule 3(1)(a)]:** In relation to a Ministry/Department/UT, means the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** or **any bank appointed to transact business of the Government** pertaining to that Ministry/Department/UT and **officially recognised for transfer of funds to the Trustee Bank**.
- **Trustee Bank [Rule 3(1)(v)]:** Means a **banking company** as defined in the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (10 of 1949)** *(intermediary appointed by PFRDA to receive NPS funds from Nodal Offices/Accredited Banks and remit to Pension Funds/ASPs)*.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: PAO/CDDO remits contributions TO the Trustee Bank THROUGH the Accredited Bank [Rule 6(10)(ii)] — never reverse the direction!
cards.exam_trap: PAO/CDDO remits contributions TO the Trustee Bank THROUGH the Accredited Bank [Rule 6(10)(ii)] — never reverse the direction!

cards.front: [Rule 3(1)(b), 3(1)(c) & 3(1)(d) | Sub-rule / Clause] Define 'Accumulated Pension Corpus' [Rule 3(1)(b)], 'Annuity' [Rule 3(1)(c)], and 'Annuity Service Provider' [Rule 3(1)(d)].
cards.back:
- **Accumulated Pension Corpus [Rule 3(1)(b)]:** The **monetary value of the pension investments accumulated** in the Individual Pension Account (IPA) of a subscriber under NPS.
- **Annuity [Rule 3(1)(c)]:** **Periodic payment** by the Annuity Service Provider to the subscriber on purchase of an annuity plan out of the Accumulated Pension Corpus.
- **Annuity Service Provider (ASP) [Rule 3(1)(d)]:** A **life insurance company** **registered and regulated by IRDAI** (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority) AND **empanelled by the Authority (PFRDA)** for providing Annuity services to NPS subscribers.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: An ASP has dual regulatory linkage: registered & regulated by IRDAI + empanelled by PFRDA.
cards.exam_trap: An ASP has dual regulatory linkage: registered & regulated by IRDAI + empanelled by PFRDA.

cards.front: [Rule 3(1)(e), 3(1)(f), 3(1)(q) & 3(1)(s) | Authority] Match each NPS entity in Rule 3(1) with its exact section of the PFRDA Act, 2013 (23 of 2013): (1) Authority [3(1)(e)], (2) Central Recordkeeping Agency [3(1)(f)], (3) National Pension System [3(1)(q)], and (4) Pension Fund [3(1)(s)].
cards.back:
1. **Authority [Rule 3(1)(e)]:** PFRDA established under **Section 3(1)** of the PFRDA Act, 2013 — *and explicitly includes the interim PFRDA set up by Central Government through Resolutions*.
2. **Central Recordkeeping Agency (CRA) [Rule 3(1)(f)]:** Agency registered under **Section 27** of PFRDA Act, 2013 (for recordkeeping, accounting, administration & customer service).
3. **National Pension System (NPS) [Rule 3(1)(q)]:** Contributory pension system referred to in **Section 20** of PFRDA Act, 2013.
4. **Pension Fund [Rule 3(1)(s)]:** Intermediary granted certificate of registration under **Section 27(3)** of PFRDA Act, 2013.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Memorize the exact section quartet: Authority = Sec 3(1); NPS = Sec 20; CRA = Sec 27; Pension Fund = Sec 27(3) of PFRDA Act, 2013 (Act 23 of 2013).
cards.exam_trap: Memorize the exact section quartet: Authority = Sec 3(1); NPS = Sec 20; CRA = Sec 27; Pension Fund = Sec 27(3) of PFRDA Act, 2013 (Act 23 of 2013).

cards.front: [Rule 3(1)(g) & 3(1)(h) | Authority] How do the definitions of 'Drawing and Disbursing Officer' (DDO) [Rule 3(1)(g)] and 'Cheque Drawing and Disbursing Officer' (CDDO) [Rule 3(1)(h)] differ?
cards.back:
- **DDO [Rule 3(1)(g)]:** Means a **Head of Office** and also any other **Gazetted Officer** so designated by a Central Govt Department, a Head of Department, or an Administrator, to draw bills and make payments on behalf of Central Govt. *Also includes a HOD or Administrator where he himself discharges such function.*
- **CDDO [Rule 3(1)(h)]:** A DDO functioning under a Ministry/Department (**including CPWD, Forest Department, and Departments authorised to follow Central Public Works Account Code**) or a UT, who is authorised to withdraw money for specified types of payments against an **assignment account** opened in his favour in a specified branch of an **accredited bank**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Key keywords for CDDO: (1) CPWD, Forest Dept, CPWA Code depts; (2) withdraws against an 'assignment account' in an accredited bank.
cards.exam_trap: Key keywords for CDDO: (1) CPWD, Forest Dept, CPWA Code depts; (2) withdraws against an 'assignment account' in an accredited bank.

cards.front: [Rule 3(1)(i) | Sub-rule / Clause] How is 'Defence Services' defined in Rule 3(1)(i) of the CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021?
cards.back:
**'Defence Services'** means services under the Government of India in the **Ministry of Defence** and in the **Defence Accounts Department (DAD)** under the control of the Ministry of Defence:
- Paid out of the **Defence Services Estimates**, AND
- **NOT permanently subject** to:
  1. The **Air Force Act, 1950** (45 of 1950), or
  2. The **Army Act, 1950** (46 of 1950), or
  3. The **Navy Act, 1957** (62 of 1957).

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Notice DAD (Defence Accounts Department) is explicitly named, and the person must NOT be permanently subject to the Army/Air Force/Navy Acts.
cards.exam_trap: Notice DAD (Defence Accounts Department) is explicitly named, and the person must NOT be permanently subject to the Army/Air Force/Navy Acts.

cards.front: [Rule 3(1)(k) & 3(1)(p) | Sub-rule / Clause] Define 'Foreign Service' [Rule 3(1)(k)] and 'Local Fund administered by Government' [Rule 3(1)(p)].
cards.back:
- **Foreign Service [Rule 3(1)(k)]:** Service in which a Government servant receives his pay **with the sanction of the Government** from **any source OTHER THAN** the Consolidated Fund of India, Consolidated Fund of a State, or Consolidated Fund of a Union territory *(note: 'Foreign Service' does NOT necessarily mean outside India — e.g., deputation to a PSU/Autonomous Body inside India paid from its own funds is Foreign Service!).*
- **Local Fund administered by Government [Rule 3(1)(p)]:** Fund administered by a body which, by law or rule having the force of law, comes under the control of the Government and over whose expenditure the Government retains **complete and direct control**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Classic FR/Pension trap: Service in a PSU/Autonomous Body in Delhi paid from PSU funds is 'Foreign Service' because pay does not come from Consolidated Fund of India/State/UT!
cards.exam_trap: Classic FR/Pension trap: Service in a PSU/Autonomous Body in Delhi paid from PSU funds is 'Foreign Service' because pay does not come from Consolidated Fund of India/State/UT!

cards.front: [Rule 3(1)(m) & 3(1)(n) | Authority] Contrast 'Head of Department' [Rule 3(1)(m)] and 'Head of Office' [Rule 3(1)(n)] with respect to DFPR, 1978 references and designating authorities.
cards.back:
| Feature | Head of Department [Rule 3(1)(m)] | Head of Office [Rule 3(1)(n)] |
|---|---|---|
| **DFPR, 1978 Provision** | **Schedule I** to DFPR, 1978 | **Rule 14** of DFPR, 1978 (must be a **Gazetted Officer**) |
| **Additional Designating Authority** | Such other authority/person whom the **President** may, by order, specify | Such other authority/person whom the **Competent Authority** may, by order, specify |

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: High-yield contrast: HOD = Schedule I DFPR + President; HOO = Rule 14 DFPR (Gazetted Officer) + Competent Authority.
cards.exam_trap: High-yield contrast: HOD = Schedule I DFPR + President; HOO = Rule 14 DFPR (Gazetted Officer) + Competent Authority.

cards.front: [Rule 3(1)(j), (l), (o), (r), (t), (u) & Rule 3(2) | Sub-rule / Clause] State the statutory definitions of IPA [3(1)(o)], PAO [3(1)(r)], PRAN [3(1)(t)], Subscriber [3(1)(u)], and the residual interpretation rule in Rule 3(2).
cards.back:
- **Emoluments [3(1)(j)]:** Emoluments as specified in **Rule 5**.
- **Government [3(1)(l)]:** Means the **Central Government**.
- **Individual Pension Account (IPA) [3(1)(o)]:** Account of a subscriber, **executed by a contract** setting out the terms and conditions under NPS.
- **Pay and Accounts Officer (PAO) [3(1)(r)]:** Officer (whatever his official designation) maintaining accounts of a Ministry/Dept/Office of Central Govt or UT, and **includes an Accountant-General**.
- **PRAN [3(1)(t)]:** Unique identification number allotted to each subscriber by the **CRA**.
- **Subscriber [3(1)(u)]:** A Government servant who subscribes to a scheme of a Pension fund.
- **Residual Definitions [Rule 3(2)]:** Undefined words/expressions carry meanings assigned in **(1) FR, 1922**, **(2) CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972 [now 2021]**, **(3) PFRDA Act, 2013**, or **(4) PFRDA Regulations**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Note that PAO explicitly includes an Accountant-General (AG), and IPA is defined as an account 'executed by a contract'.
cards.exam_trap: Note that PAO explicitly includes an Accountant-General (AG), and IPA is defined as an account 'executed by a contract'.

cards.front: [Rule 2(a) & G.S.R. 735(E) dt. 01.10.2025 | 2024–2026 Update] Why are 'Railway servants' excluded under Rule 2(a) of CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021, and which latest statutory rules now govern them?
cards.back:
Railway servants are excluded from CCS Rules under **Rule 2(a)**. Their NPS service matters are now statutorily governed by the **Railway Services (Implementation of National Pension System) Rules, 2025**, notified vide **G.S.R. 735(E) dated 01.10.2025** (circulated vide Railway Board **RBE No. 103/2025 dated 08.10.2025**).

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Do NOT confuse CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021 [G.S.R. 227(E)] with Railway Services (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2025 [G.S.R. 735(E)].
cards.exam_trap: Do NOT confuse CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021 [G.S.R. 227(E)] with Railway Services (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2025 [G.S.R. 735(E)].

cards.front: [Rule 2(d) & G.S.R. 307(E) dt. 22.04.2026 | 2024–2026 Update] Members of All India Services (IAS/IPS/IFoS) are excluded under Rule 2(d) of CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021. Which 2026 statutory rules now govern them?
cards.back:
All India Services officers appointed on or after 01.01.2004 are now governed by the **All India Services (Implementation of National Pension System) Rules, 2026**, notified by DoPT under **Section 3(1) of the All India Services Act, 1951** vide **G.S.R. 307(E) dated 22.04.2026**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Notice the enacting statute difference: CCS NPS Rules 2021 = Art. 309 Proviso + Art. 148(5); AIS NPS Rules 2026 = Section 3(1) of AIS Act, 1951!
cards.exam_trap: Notice the enacting statute difference: CCS NPS Rules 2021 = Art. 309 Proviso + Art. 148(5); AIS NPS Rules 2026 = Section 3(1) of AIS Act, 1951!

cards.front: [Rule 2(e) | Exception] Are Indian citizens or foreign nationals 'locally recruited' for Indian Embassies / Consulates abroad covered by CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021?
cards.back:
**NO.** Under **Rule 2(e)**, *'persons locally recruited for services in diplomatic, consular or other Indian establishments in foreign countries'* are **expressly excluded** from the CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021 *(unlike regular India-based MEA officials posted abroad, who ARE covered)*.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Distinguish 'locally recruited staff in Indian missions abroad' [excluded under Rule 2(e)] from 'India-based subscribers posted abroad' [covered by the Rules, though barred from VRS while posted abroad under Rule 12(1) Proviso (ii)]!
cards.exam_trap: Distinguish 'locally recruited staff in Indian missions abroad' [excluded under Rule 2(e)] from 'India-based subscribers posted abroad' [covered by the Rules, though barred from VRS while posted abroad under Rule 12(1) Proviso (ii)]!

cards.front: [Rule 3(1)(a) | Sub-rule / Clause] [Clause Drill — Rule 3(1)(a)] Can the Reserve Bank of India itself be an 'Accredited Bank' under Rule 3(1)(a)?
cards.back:
**YES.** Under **Rule 3(1)(a)**, *'Accredited Bank'* in relation to a Ministry/Department/UT means **the Reserve Bank** OR any bank appointed to transact Government business pertaining to that Ministry/Department/UT and officially recognised for transfer of funds to the Trustee Bank.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Many candidates assume only commercial agency banks (like SBI) are Accredited Banks — Rule 3(1)(a) explicitly begins with 'means the Reserve Bank or any bank...'.
cards.exam_trap: Many candidates assume only commercial agency banks (like SBI) are Accredited Banks — Rule 3(1)(a) explicitly begins with 'means the Reserve Bank or any bank...'.

cards.front: [Rule 3(1)(e) | Sub-rule / Clause] [Clause Drill — Rule 3(1)(e)] Does the definition of 'Authority' in Rule 3(1)(e) cover actions of the pre-2013 interim PFRDA?
cards.back:
**YES.** **Rule 3(1)(e)** defines *'Authority'* as the PFRDA established under **Section 3(1) of the PFRDA Act, 2013 (23 of 2013)** AND explicitly **'includes interim Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority set up by the Central Government through Resolutions'**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Because NPS started on 01.01.2004 while the statutory PFRDA Act was enacted in 2013, Rule 3(1)(e) expressly includes the resolution-based Interim PFRDA.
cards.exam_trap: Because NPS started on 01.01.2004 while the statutory PFRDA Act was enacted in 2013, Rule 3(1)(e) expressly includes the resolution-based Interim PFRDA.

cards.front: [Rule 3(1)(g) | Authority] [Clause Drill — Rule 3(1)(g)] Can a Non-Gazetted officer be designated as a Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) under Rule 3(1)(g)?
cards.back:
**NO.** Under **Rule 3(1)(g)**, *'Drawing and Disbursing Officer'* means a **Head of Office** and also **any other Gazetted Officer** so designated by a Department of the Central Government, a Head of Department, or an Administrator (and includes a HOD or Administrator discharging such function himself).

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Both Head of Office [Rule 3(1)(n)] and DDO designated under Rule 3(1)(g) specify 'Gazetted Officer'!
cards.exam_trap: Both Head of Office [Rule 3(1)(n)] and DDO designated under Rule 3(1)(g) specify 'Gazetted Officer'!

cards.front: [Rule 3(1)(p) | Sub-rule / Clause] [Clause Drill — Rule 3(1)(p)] What degree of control over expenditure is required for a fund to qualify as a 'Local Fund administered by Government'?
cards.back:
Under **Rule 3(1)(p)**, the body must come under the control of the Government by law or rule having the force of law, AND over its expenditure the Government must retain **'COMPLETE AND DIRECT CONTROL'**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Partial grant-in-aid or general regulatory oversight is NOT enough — the exact statutory phrase is 'complete and direct control' over expenditure.
cards.exam_trap: Partial grant-in-aid or general regulatory oversight is NOT enough — the exact statutory phrase is 'complete and direct control' over expenditure.

cards.front: [Rule 3(2) + Statutory Updates | 2024–2026 Update] Where CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021 cite 'CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972' and 'CCS (Extraordinary Pension) Rules, 1939', which updated rules replace them today?
cards.back:

cards.front: [Rule 4(1) | Timeline / Deadline] When and in which forms must a newly appointed Government servant apply for registration into NPS under Rule 4(1)?
cards.back:

- **To Whom:** **Head of Office (HOO)**.
- **Forms to Submit Together:**
  1. **Common Subscriber Registration Form (CSRF)** (or any other form specified by PFRDA), **ALONG WITH**
  2. **Option Form referred to in Rule 10** (i.e., **Form 1** for OPS/NPS death/disability option + **Form 2** family details).

cards.front: [Rule 4(2), 4(3) & 4(4) | Timeline / Deadline] State the exact '3-3-3 Working Days' chain of timelines from joining to CRA submission under Rule 4(2), Rule 4(3), and Rule 4(4).
cards.back:
1. **HOO → DDO [Rule 4(2)]:** Within **3 working days of joining** of the Government servant (HOO ensures completeness, countersigns with date of receipt, keeps a copy for record, sends to DDO).
2. **DDO → PAO / CDDO [Rule 4(3)]:** Within **3 working days from the date of receipt** of application from HOO.
3. **PAO / CDDO → CRA [Rule 4(4)]:** Within **3 working days from the date of receipt** of application from DDO (processed & forwarded via **online system**, PLUS a duly signed copy forwarded to CRA for record).

cards.front: [Rule 4(5), 4(6), 4(7) & 4(8) | Timeline / Deadline] Trace the reverse communication chain once CRA generates PRAN under Rule 4(5)–(8), including the exact working-day deadline for Service Book entry.

- **Rule 4(5) [CRA]:** Completes registration & allocates PRAN as per PFRDA Turn-Around Time (TAT); communicates PRAN to PAO/CDDO AND forwards **PRAN kit** to Subscriber.
- **Rule 4(6) [PAO/CDDO → DDO]:** Communicates PRAN to DDO **immediately**.
- **Rule 4(7) [DDO → HOO]:** Communicates PRAN to HOO **immediately**.
- **Rule 4(8) [HOO → Subscriber & Service Book]:** HOO intimates PRAN to Subscriber, records PRAN in CSRF & Service Book, AND pastes a **certified copy of CSRF** in the Service Book **within 5 working days thereafter**.

cards.front: [Rule 4(9) | Timeline / Deadline] What is the outer statutory deadline for crediting the FIRST contribution of a Government servant into his Individual Pension Account under Rule 4(9)?
cards.back:
The **first contribution** of the Government servant shall be credited in his Individual Pension Account:
- **Within 20 days** of the date of submission of the application under Rule 4(1), **OR**
- **By the last date of the month** in which the Government servant joined,
- **WHICHEVER IS LATER**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: SUPER COMMON EXAM TRAP: Rule 4(9) says 'whichever is LATER' (NOT 'whichever is earlier'). Example: Joins & submits CSRF on 2nd May -> 20 days is 22nd May, last date of month is 31st May -> deadline is 31st May! Joins on 25th May -> 20 days is 14th June -> deadline is 14th June!
cards.exam_trap: SUPER COMMON EXAM TRAP: Rule 4(9) says 'whichever is LATER' (NOT 'whichever is earlier'). Example: Joins & submits CSRF on 2nd May -> 20 days is 22nd May, last date of month is 31st May -> deadline is 31st May! Joins on 25th May -> 20 days is 14th June -> deadline is 14th June!

cards.front: [Rule 4(10) & 4(11) | Exception] What happens under Rule 4(10) if a newly joined Government servant's NPS registration / PRAN generation is NOT completed before drawal of his first or subsequent month's salary?
cards.back:
1. **Salary MUST NOT be stopped!** Salary for the first month (or any subsequent month) **shall be paid** to the Government servant **after withholding the amount of subscriber contribution** determined under Rule 6 (10% of emoluments).
2. **Subsequent Credit with Interest:** As soon as PRAN generation is completed by CRA and communicated to PAO/CDDO, the **withheld contribution ALONG WITH interest payable under Rule 8** (at PPF rate) shall be credited to his Individual Pension Account.
3. **Rule 4(11):** Action on the option form submitted under Rule 4(1) is taken as per **Rule 10**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Prior to 2021 Rules, some offices held up first salary awaiting PRAN. Rule 4(10) mandates paying net salary after withholding 10% NPS contribution and later crediting it WITH Rule 8 interest!
cards.exam_trap: Prior to 2021 Rules, some offices held up first salary awaiting PRAN. Rule 4(10) mandates paying net salary after withholding 10% NPS contribution and later crediting it WITH Rule 8 interest!

cards.front: [Rule 4(9) — Numerical Case Study | Exam Trap] [Case Study — Rule 4(9)] Shri 'A' joins Central Govt service and submits his CSRF on 18th August. By which exact date MUST his first NPS contribution be credited into his IPA?
cards.back:
**7th September!**
- Under **Rule 4(9)**, first contribution must be credited within **20 days of submission of application** (18th Aug + 20 days = **7th September**) OR by the **last date of the month of joining** (**31st August**), **whichever is LATER**.
- Since **7th September** is later than 31st August, the statutory deadline is **7th September**.

cards.front: [Rule 4(2) vs Rule 4(8) | Sub-rule / Clause] Compare the Head of Office's record-keeping duties at the START of registration [Rule 4(2)] versus AFTER PRAN allotment [Rule 4(8)].

- **After PRAN Allotment [Rule 4(8)]:** Within **5 working days** after receiving PRAN from DDO, HOO intimates PRAN to Subscriber, **records PRAN in CSRF AND in the Service Book**, and **pastes a CERTIFIED COPY of CSRF in the Service Book**.

cards.front: [Rule 4(9) Opening Sentence, Rule 4(10) & Rule 4(11) | Sub-rule / Clause] [Sub-rule Drill — Rule 4(9)–(11)] Separate the exact statutory mandates of: (a) Opening sentence of Rule 4(9), (b) First & second sentences of Rule 4(10), and (c) Rule 4(11)!
cards.back:
- **(a) Joint No-Delay Mandate [Rule 4(9), 1st Sentence]:** Casts an explicit statutory obligation on **ALL authorities referred to in sub-rules (2) to (8)** *(HOO, DDO, PAO, CDDO, and CRA)* to ensure there is **no delay** in registration and crediting of first contribution.
- **(b) Uncompleted Registration — Salary Release + Delayed Credit [Rule 4(10)]:**
  - *1st Sentence:* If registration is not completed before drawal of **first month's or any subsequent month's salary**, such salary/salaries **SHALL BE PAID** after **withholding 10% contribution** determined under Rule 6.
  - *2nd Sentence:* The **withheld contribution + interest payable under Rule 8** (PPF rate) **SHALL BE CREDITED** to the IPA **as soon as** PRAN generation is completed by CRA and communicated to PAO/CDDO.
- **(c) Rule 10 Cross-Link [Rule 4(11)]:** Action on the **Option Form** submitted at joining under Rule 4(1) shall be taken in accordance with **Rule 10**.

cards.front: [Rule 5(1) | Formula / Rate] What exact components constitute 'Emoluments' for mandatory NPS contributions under Rule 5(1)?
cards.back:
For determining mandatory contribution in a calendar month, **'Emoluments'** includes ONLY THREE elements:
1. **Basic Pay** as defined in **FR 9(21)(a)(i)** (Fundamental Rules, 1922),
2. **Non-Practicing Allowance (NPA)** granted to a medical officer in lieu of private practice, AND
3. **Admissible Dearness Allowance (DA)** in a calendar month.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Compare with CCS (Pension) Rules / Gratuity Rules! In CCS (Pension) Rules, emoluments = Basic Pay + NPA (NO DA for pension, though DA counts for Gratuity). Under CCS (NPS) Rule 5(1), Emoluments = Basic Pay + NPA + DA! HRA, Transport Allowance, Special Pay, Deputation (Duty) Allowance are EXCLUDED.
cards.exam_trap: Compare with CCS (Pension) Rules / Gratuity Rules! In CCS (Pension) Rules, emoluments = Basic Pay + NPA (NO DA for pension, though DA counts for Gratuity). Under CCS (NPS) Rule 5(1), Emoluments = Basic Pay + NPA + DA! HRA, Transport Allowance, Special Pay, Deputation (Duty) Allowance are EXCLUDED.

cards.front: [Rule 5(2) & 5(3) | Sub-rule / Clause] How are 'Emoluments' calculated when a Subscriber is (a) on paid leave [Rule 5(2)], or (b) absent from duty / on Extraordinary Leave (EOL) during whole or part of a calendar month [Rule 5(3)]?
cards.back:
Both sub-rules operate **subject to the Proviso to Rule 7(1)**:
- **Paid Leave [Rule 5(2)]:** The amount representing **Pay, NPA, and DA actually drawn** in the leave salary during leave is taken as emoluments *(e.g., on Half Pay Leave, actual half-pay leave salary + admissible DA/NPA drawn)*.
- **Absence / EOL for whole or part of month [Rule 5(3)]:** The Pay (or Pay + NPA + DA in leave salary) **actually drawn for that part of the calendar month** during which he was on duty or on paid leave is taken as emoluments *(if on normal EOL for entire month without medical/civil commotion/study ground, emoluments = NIL)*.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Always check if the leave falls under the 3 special exceptions in Proviso to Rule 7(1) (medical ground, civil commotion, useful higher studies) — if yes, Government pays 14% on NOTIONAL full emoluments even if leave salary is nil or half!
cards.exam_trap: Always check if the leave falls under the 3 special exceptions in Proviso to Rule 7(1) (medical ground, civil commotion, useful higher studies) — if yes, Government pays 14% on NOTIONAL full emoluments even if leave salary is nil or half!

cards.front: [Rule 5(4) | Sub-rule / Clause] What constitutes 'Emoluments' for a Subscriber placed under suspension under Rule 5(4)?
cards.back:
Under **Rule 5(4)**, if a Subscriber has been under suspension, the **subsistence allowance drawn** during the period of suspension in a calendar month *(including DA admissible on subsistence allowance)* shall be taken into account as emoluments *(applicable where the Subscriber opts to contribute during suspension under Rule 6(2))*.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: During suspension, contribution is OPTIONAL for the Subscriber [Rule 6(2)]. If he opts in, both 10% and 14% are calculated on Subsistence Allowance drawn; if he opts out, Govt also pays NIL [Rule 7(3) 1st Proviso].
cards.exam_trap: During suspension, contribution is OPTIONAL for the Subscriber [Rule 6(2)]. If he opts in, both 10% and 14% are calculated on Subsistence Allowance drawn; if he opts out, Govt also pays NIL [Rule 7(3) 1st Proviso].

cards.front: [Rule 5(5) vs Rule 5(6) | Exam Trap] Contrast how 'Emoluments' are reckoned during (a) Deputation IN India [Rule 5(5)] versus (b) Foreign Service or Deputation OUTSIDE India [Rule 5(6)].
cards.back:
- **Deputation IN India [Rule 5(5)]:** **Actual pay drawn** by the Subscriber while on deputation in India (+ DA) is taken into account for emoluments.
- **Foreign Service OR Deputation OUTSIDE India [Rule 5(6)]:** **Notional pay** — i.e., the pay which he **would have drawn under the Government had he NOT been on foreign service or such deputation** (+ admissible DA) is taken into account!

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: A-grade exam trap! Note that 'Foreign Service' [Rule 3(1)(k)] includes deputation to an Indian PSU/Autonomous Body! Under Rule 5(6), BOTH Foreign Service (even within India!) AND Deputation outside India use NOTIONAL parent-cadre pay, whereas Deputation in India (to Central/State Govt) under Rule 5(5) uses ACTUAL pay drawn!

AND Deputation outside India use NOTIONAL parent-cadre pay, whereas Deputation in India (to Central/State Govt) under Rule 5(5) uses ACTUAL pay drawn!

cards.front: [Rule 5(7) | Sub-rule / Clause] How are 'Emoluments' calculated for a retired Subscriber who is re-employed in Government service with pay reduced by pension [Rule 5(7)]?
cards.back:
Under **Rule 5(7)**, where a retired Subscriber is re-employed in Government service (to whom these rules apply) and his **pay on re-employment has been reduced by an amount not exceeding his monthly pension**:
- The **element of monthly pension by which his pay is reduced SHALL BE INCLUDED in emoluments** *(i.e., Reduced Pay + Ignored/Deducted Pension Element = Full Fixation Pay + admissible DA)*.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Do NOT calculate NPS contribution merely on 'net re-employment pay minus pension' — the deducted pension component must be added back to arrive at Emoluments!

cards.front: [Rule 5(1) & 6(1)/7(1) — Numerical Case Study | Formula / Rate] [Numerical Case Study — Rules 5(1), 6(1) & 7(1)] A Central Govt Medical Officer draws Basic Pay ₹67,700, NPA ₹13,540 (20%), DA @ 53% on (Pay + NPA) = ₹43,057.20 → ₹43,057, HRA ₹21,935, and Transport Allowance ₹11,016. Compute his exact monthly Employee (10%) and Govt (14%) NPS contributions!
cards.back:
1. **Emoluments [Rule 5(1)]:** Basic Pay (`₹67,700`) + NPA (`₹13,540`) + DA (`₹43,057`) = **`₹1,24,297`** *(HRA & Transport Allowance are EXCLUDED)*.
2. **Subscriber Contribution @ 10% [Rule 6(1)]:** `10% of ₹1,24,297 = ₹12,429.70` → Rounded to **NEXT HIGHER RUPEE** = **`₹12,430`**.
3. **Government Contribution @ 14% [Rule 7(1)]:** `14% of ₹1,24,297 = ₹17,401.58` → Rounded to **NEXT HIGHER RUPEE** = **`₹17,402`**.
*(Note: Even if 10% had been `₹12,429.10`, rounding to next higher rupee still gives `₹12,430`!)*

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Always exclude HRA, TA, Dress Allowance, Special Allowance, CEA; include ONLY Basic Pay [FR 9(21)(a)(i)] + NPA + DA, and round UP any fraction > .00 to the next integer rupee!
cards.exam_trap: Always exclude HRA, TA, Dress Allowance, Special Allowance, CEA; include ONLY Basic Pay [FR 9(21)(a)(i)] + NPA + DA, and round UP any fraction > .00 to the next integer rupee!

cards.front: [Rule 5(5) & 5(6) — Case Study | Exam Trap] [Case Study — Rule 5(5) vs 5(6)] Compare NPS 'Emoluments' of Officer X (on deputation to State Govt of Karnataka drawing higher deputation pay) vs Officer Y (on foreign service in NHAI / a Central PSU drawing higher PSU pay).
cards.back:
- **Officer X (Deputation to State Govt in India) [Rule 5(5) & 6(4)]:** Governed by **Rule 5(5)** → **Actual pay drawn** on deputation in Karnataka (+ DA) is taken as Emoluments.
- **Officer Y (Foreign Service in NHAI / PSU) [Rule 5(6) & 3(1)(k)]:** Because pay is drawn from NHAI/PSU funds (NOT Consolidated Fund of India/State/UT), it is **Foreign Service** [Rule 3(1)(k)]. Under **Rule 5(6)**, **Notional pay** which Officer Y **would have drawn in parent Government cadre** had he not been on foreign service (+ DA) is taken as Emoluments!

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: This is the #1 conceptual trap in Rule 5: 'Foreign service' in Rule 5(6) applies to domestic PSUs/Autonomous Bodies too, not just postings abroad!
cards.exam_trap: This is the #1 conceptual trap in Rule 5: 'Foreign service' in Rule 5(6) applies to domestic PSUs/Autonomous Bodies too, not just postings abroad!

cards.front: [Rule 5(1) read with FR 9(21)(a)(i) | Exam Trap] Rule 5(1) defines Basic Pay strictly by reference to 'FR 9(21)(a)(i)'. Which components of FR 9(21)(a) are thereby EXCLUDED from NPS Emoluments?
cards.back:
- **INCLUDED — `FR 9(21)(a)(i)`:** Pay (other than special pay or pay granted in view of personal qualifications) sanctioned for a post held substantively or in an officiating capacity *(i.e., Pay in the Pay Matrix)*.
- **EXCLUDED — `FR 9(21)(a)(ii)` & `(iii)`:**
  1. **Special Pay** and **Personal Pay** [`FR 9(21)(a)(ii)`],
  2. **Any other emoluments specially classed as pay** by the President [`FR 9(21)(a)(iii)`],
  3. **Deputation (Duty) Allowance**, **Special Allowance**, **HRA**, **Transport Allowance**, **Overtime/Honorarium**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Favourite SAS/AAO Paper trap: Special Pay and Personal Pay fall under FR 9(21)(a)(ii), NOT FR 9(21)(a)(i), so they do NOT count for 10%/14% NPS contribution!

cards.front: [Rule 6(1) & Rule 7(1), 7(5) | Formula / Rate] What are the mandatory monthly contribution percentages of (a) the Subscriber [Rule 6(1)] and (b) the Government [Rule 7(1)], and what is the exact statutory rounding-off rule?
cards.back:
- **Basis:** Defined contribution basis [Rule 6(1)].
- **Subscriber's Mandatory Contribution [Rule 6(1)]:** **10%** (or such other % notified from time to time) of monthly emoluments.
- **Government's Mandatory Contribution [Rule 7(1)]:** **14%** (or such other % notified from time to time; raised from 10% to 14% w.e.f. **01.04.2019**) of monthly emoluments.
- **Rounding-Off Rule [Rule 6(1) & Rule 7(1), 7(5)]:** Both Subscriber and Government contributions **shall be rounded off to the NEXT HIGHER RUPEE** *(even 1 paisa fraction rounds UP — e.g., ₹5,420.05 → ₹5,421)*.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: BIG NUMERICAL TRAP: Rounding is NOT 'nearest rupee' (50 paise rule) — it is ALWAYS 'NEXT HIGHER RUPEE' for both 10% employee and 14% employer contributions!
cards.exam_trap: BIG NUMERICAL TRAP: Rounding is NOT 'nearest rupee' (50 paise rule) — it is ALWAYS 'NEXT HIGHER RUPEE' for both 10% employee and 14% employer contributions!

cards.front: [Rule 6(2) & Rule 7(3) + 1st & 2nd Provisos | Proviso] Explain the complete three-part legal position on Subscriber and Government NPS contributions during SUSPENSION and upon conclusion of inquiry [Rule 6(2) & Rule 7(3) with Provisos].
cards.back:
1. **During Suspension — Subscriber's Option [Rule 6(2) & Rule 7(3)]:**
   - Subscriber **MAY, at his option**, contribute 10% based on subsistence allowance.
   - If Subscriber contributes, Government contributes **14%** based on subsistence allowance [Rule 7(3)].
   - **1st Proviso to Rule 7(3):** **NO contribution shall be made by the Government** during suspension where the Subscriber **opted NOT to pay** his contribution!
2. **On Conclusion of Inquiry — Period Treated as Duty or Paid Leave [Proviso to Rule 6(2) & 2nd Proviso to Rule 7(3)]:**
   - Both Subscriber (10%) and Government (14%) contributions are recalculated on the **emoluments to which the Subscriber becomes entitled** for the suspension period.
   - The **difference** (entitled contribution minus contribution already deposited during suspension) **shall be credited** to the IPA **ALONG WITH INTEREST at the Public Provident Fund (PPF) deposit rate**!

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Notice TWO traps: (1) If employee opts out during suspension, Govt pays ZERO during suspension; (2) On exoneration / period treated as duty or paid leave, BOTH employee difference and Govt difference carry PPF rate interest!

cards.front: [Rule 6(3), Rule 7(1) Proviso & Rule 7(2) | Proviso] State the THREE exceptional kinds of leave under the Proviso to Rule 7(1) where the Government MUST pay 14% contribution on NOTIONAL full emoluments even when leave salary is NIL (EOL) or less than full pay (e.g. HPL)!
cards.back:
**General Rule [Rule 6(3) & Rule 7(2)]:** During absence/leave where **no pay or leave salary is payable**, Subscriber pays **NIL** [Rule 6(3)] and ordinarily Government also pays **NIL** [Rule 7(2)].

**CRITICAL EXCEPTION — Proviso to Rule 7(1):** Where leave is granted to the Subscriber:
1. On **medical ground**, OR
2. Due to **inability to join or rejoin duty on account of civil commotion**, OR
3. For **pursuing higher studies considered useful in discharge of his official duty**,
AND during such leave **leave salary is NOT payable (EOL) or is payable at LESS than full pay (e.g., Half Pay Leave)**:
- **Government SHALL make 14% contribution** on **NOTIONAL EMOLUMENTS** (full Pay + DA + NPA under Rule 5)!
- *(Meanwhile, under Rule 6(3) & 5(2), Subscriber pays NIL on EOL, or 10% only on actual reduced leave salary drawn on HPL!)*

cards.front: [Rule 6(4), 6(5), 6(6), 6(7), 6(9) & Rule 7(4) | Sub-rule / Clause] What do Rules 6(4)–6(7), 6(9), and 7(4) prescribe regarding NPS contributions during: (a) Deputation in India, (b) Salary Arrears, (c) Probation, (d) Foreign Service / UN / International Orgs, and (e) Voluntary Excess Contribution?
cards.back:
- **(a) Deputation to Central/State Govt Dept/Org [Rule 6(4)]:** Subscriber remains subject to these rules as if not transferred and continues contributing based on Rule 5(5) emoluments (actual pay drawn).
- **(b) Retrospective Salary Arrears [Rule 6(5)]:** Contributions on arrears of salary due to retrospective increase **shall be treated as contributions for the month in which the payments are made**.
- **(c) Probation Period [Rule 6(6)]:** Subscriber **SHALL contribute** towards NPS during probation.
- **(d) Foreign Service in/outside India & UN/IMF/IBRD/ADB/Commonwealth Secretariat/International Orgs [Rule 6(7) & Rule 7(4)]:** Regulated as per **DoPT instructions/orders** and **PFRDA procedure**.
- **(e) Voluntary Excess Contribution [Rule 6(9)]:** Subscriber **may, at his option**, contribute **in excess of 10%** specified in Rule 6(1) per PFRDA & Govt procedure.

cards.front: [Rule 6(8), Rule 6(10)(i)–(iii) & Rule 7(6) | Timeline / Deadline] Give the exact monthly calendar milestones ('20th — 25th — Last Working Day') for NPS deduction, SCF upload, and bank remittance under Rule 6(8), Rule 6(10), and Rule 7(6), INCLUDING the March Proviso!
cards.back:
1. **On or before 20th day of each month [Rule 6(8)]:** **DDO** deducts contribution from salary and sends the salary bill + subscriber-wise contribution details to **PAO / CDDO**.
2. **By 25th day of each month [Rule 6(10)(i)]:** **PAO / CDDO** prepares & uploads the **Subscription Contribution File (SCF)** and generates a **Transaction ID**.
3. **By the LAST working day of each month [Rule 6(10)(ii)]:** **PAO / CDDO** remits the contribution to the **Trustee Bank through the Accredited Bank**.
4. **MARCH EXCEPTION [Proviso to Rule 6(10)(ii)]:** Contribution for the month of **March** shall be remitted to the Trustee Bank through the Accredited Bank on the **FIRST WORKING DAY OF APRIL**!
5. **Delayed Credit Compensation [Rule 6(10)(iii)]:** Where there is a delay in crediting Subscriber's contribution to the IPA beyond the prescribed timeline **due to factors not attributable to the Subscriber**, the amount shall be credited along with **interest for the delayed period under Rule 8** (at PPF deposit rate).
6. **Rule 7(6):** Identical remittance timelines & Rule 8 interest on delay apply to the **14% Government contribution**.

cards.front: [Rule 8(1) & Proviso to Rule 8(1) | Formula / Rate] Under Rule 8(1), for which delays is interest payable to the Subscriber, at what rate, within what time limit, and what is the Proviso for the period 01.01.2004 to 31.12.2012?
cards.back:
**Three Covered Delays (due to factors NOT attributable to Subscriber) [Rule 8(1)(i)–(iii)]:**
- **(i)** Delay in commencement of monthly contributions due to registration delay beyond **Rule 4** timelines;
- **(ii)** Delay in deduction/crediting of Subscriber's monthly contribution beyond **Rule 6** timeline;
- **(iii)** Delay in crediting Government's monthly contribution beyond **Rule 7** timeline.

**Time Limit to Credit Interest:** **Within 30 days** of the crediting of the amount of contribution.
**Rate of Interest:** Rate decided by Government from time to time for **Public Provident Fund (PPF) deposits**.
**PROVISO (2004–2012 Legacy Period):** For **01.01.2004 to 31.12.2012**, rate of interest is as notified by **Dept. of Financial Services Notification F.No. 1/3/2016-PR dt. 31.01.2019** and **Dept. of Expenditure OM No. 1(21)/EV/2018 dt. 12.04.2019** *(GPF rates)*.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Do NOT confuse GPF rate with PPF rate! Under Rule 8(1) (and Rules 6(2)/7(3)), current delayed-deposit interest rate is PPF deposit rate (NOT GPF rate, except for the 2004–2012 proviso), and must be credited within 30 days of crediting the principal contribution!

cards.front: [Rule 8(2)(i), 8(2)(ii) & 8(2)(iii) | Authority] Who fixes responsibility for delayed NPS registration/contributions under Rule 8(2), who bears the pecuniary loss, and which exact Income-tax Act provision governs determination of liability?
cards.back:
- **Examining Authorities [Rule 8(2)(i)]:** Every case of delay under Rule 4, Rule 6, or Rule 7 **shall be examined by the Head of Department (HOD) OR Chief Controller of Accounts (CCA)** for fixation of responsibility.
- **Personal Pecuniary Recovery [Rule 8(2)(ii)]:** If HOD or CCA is satisfied that delay is due to **administrative lapse**, the **delinquent official(s) shall be liable to pay the amount of pecuniary loss** to the Government on account of payment of interest.
- **Statutory Yardstick [Rule 8(2)(iii)]:** Responsibility and amount of liability shall be determined in the **same manner as delayed deduction or remittance of TDS under Section 201(1A) [printed as 'sub-section (IA) of section 201' in Gazette] of the Income-tax Act, 1961** *(corresponding to Sec. 397(3) of Income-tax Act, 2025)* — *without prejudice to any disciplinary action*.

  1. **Direct Voluntary Contribution (`eNPS` / PoP into Tier-I or Tier-II):** Subscriber can deposit any voluntary amount directly into his PRAN (eligible for **₹50,000** additional deduction in Old Tax Regime under **Sec. 80CCD(1B)** of 1961 Act / **Sec. 124(3)** of Income-tax Act, 2025).

  - **(ii)** Subscriber **SHALL be given an opportunity to submit a FRESH option** at the time of discharge!

cards.front: [Rule 10(6)(i), (ii) & (iii) + DoPPW OM dt. 25.10.2024 | Exception] What is the statutory 'Default Option' under Rule 10(6)(i), (ii), and (iii) when a Subscriber dies or is invalidated/disabled WITHOUT having exercised any option in Form 1 (and how did the position shift after March 2024)?

   - **Before completion of 15 years of service**, **OR**

cards.front: [Rule 10(7) | Exception] What happens under Rule 10(7) if a deceased Subscriber had opted (or defaulted) for OPS / EOP Family Pension, but NO family member is eligible for Family Pension under CCS (Pension) / (EOP) Rules?
cards.back:
Under **Rule 10(7)** [Infructuous Option Clause]:
- Where the exercised option [Rule 10(1)] or default option [Rule 10(6)] for benefits under CCS (Pension) Rules or CCS (EOP) Rules **becomes infructuous on account of non-availability of an eligible member of the family for grant of family pension**:
  1. Such OPS/EOP option **shall be deemed to have become INVALID**, AND
  2. **Benefits admissible under the National Pension System (full Accumulated Pension Corpus)** shall be granted to the **legal heir(s)** of the deceased employee under PFRDA (Exits & Withdrawals) Regulations, 2015!

cards.front: [Rule 11 | Sub-rule / Clause] What are the NPS exit entitlements of a Subscriber retiring on superannuation (or after extension of service beyond superannuation) under Rule 11?
cards.back:
Under **Rule 11**, a Subscriber who retires on attaining the age of superannuation — or, where service was extended beyond superannuation, **on expiry of such period of extension** — is entitled to benefits admissible under the **PFRDA (Exits and Withdrawals under National Pension System) Regulations, 2015** to a Subscriber retiring on superannuation.

*(Latest PFRDA Govt Sector Superannuation Norms [16.12.2025 Amendment]: Corpus **> ₹12 Lakh** → up to **60% lump sum** + min **40% annuity**; Corpus **₹8L–₹12L** → up to ₹6L lump sum + SUR/SLW/Annuity [or 60:40]; Corpus **≤ ₹8 Lakh** [raised from ₹5L] → **100% lump sum** permitted! Cross-read with **FR 56(a)** via **Rule 29(1)**: retirement takes effect on the afternoon of the last day of the month of attaining superannuation age, and a Government servant **born on the 1st day of a month** retires on the afternoon of the **last day of the preceding month**!)*

cards.front: [Rule 12(1) — Explanation (a), (b) & (c) | Exam Trap] Under Explanation (a), (b), and (c) to Rule 12(1), how is 'Regular Service' computed for 20-year Voluntary Retirement? Specifically, do Extraordinary Leave (EOL), Study Leave, and prior ad-hoc/contract service count?
cards.back:
- **Explanation (a) [Past Regular Service]:** Commences from joining a Central Govt post on regular basis (direct recruitment / absorption / re-employment) AND **includes past regular service** in same/another Central Govt Dept, State Govt, or Autonomous/Statutory Body joined **with proper permission**, *if such past service is allowed to be counted as qualifying service for gratuity*.
- **Explanation (b) [ALL Leave Counts!]:** Periods spent on **ALL KINDS OF LEAVE (explicitly INCLUDING Study Leave and Extraordinary Leave — EOL!)**, deputation, or foreign service duly sanctioned by competent authority **SHALL BE TREATED AS REGULAR SERVICE**!
- **Explanation (c) [Excluded Service]:** Service rendered on **casual, ad-hoc, or contract basis** before regular appointment (in Central/State Govt or AB/Statutory Body) **SHALL NOT** be treated as regular service.

cards.front: [Rule 12(2), 12(3)(a)–(b) & 12(4) + Provisos | Timeline / Deadline] Under Rule 12(2)–(4), explain: (a) Deemed acceptance of VRS notice, (b) Curtailment of 3-month notice, and (c) Withdrawal of VRS notice & its mandatory deadline.
cards.back:
- **(a) Acceptance & Deemed Acceptance [Rule 12(2) + Proviso]:** Notice requires acceptance by Appointing Authority. **Proviso:** Where Appointing Authority **does NOT refuse** permission **before expiry of the notice period**, retirement **becomes effective automatically from the date of expiry** of the said period!
- **(b) Curtailment of Notice (< 3 months) [Rule 12(3)(a)–(b)]:** Subscriber may request in writing with reasons; Appointing Authority may consider on merits and **relax/curtail the 3-month notice** if satisfied it will **not cause any administrative inconvenience**.
- **(c) Withdrawal of VRS Notice [Rule 12(4) + Proviso]:** Subscriber is precluded from withdrawing notice **except with specific approval** of Appointing Authority. **Proviso:** Request for withdrawal **SHALL BE MADE AT LEAST 15 DAYS BEFORE** the intended date of his retirement!

cards.back:
- **Excluded from Rule 12 [Rule 12(5)(a)–(b)]:** Rule 12 does NOT apply to a Subscriber who:
  - **(a)** Retires under **DoPT Special Voluntary Retirement Scheme (SVRS)** for surplus employees (*OM No. 25013/6/2001-Estt.(A) dt. 28.02.2002*) [covered by Rule 13]; or
  - **(b)** Retires from Govt service for **being absorbed in an Autonomous Body or PSU** [covered by Rule 15].
  - *Explanation:* 'Appointing authority' = authority competent to make appointments to the service/post from which Subscriber seeks VRS.
- **Exit Benefit [Rule 12(6)]:** Entitled to NPS benefits **AS ADMISSIBLE ON SUPERANNUATION (up to 60% lump sum + min 40% annuity)** — *NOT premature 20:80 exit!*
- **Continuation / Deferment [Rule 12(7)]:** May opt to continue IPA or defer benefits under PFRDA Regulations.

cards.front: [Rule 14(1) & 1st, 2nd, 3rd Provisos | Proviso] What is the NPS payout rule on ordinary Resignation from Government service under Rule 14(1), and state ALL THREE Provisos to Rule 14(1)!
cards.back:
- **Main Rule [Rule 14(1)]:** Unless resignation is allowed to be withdrawn in public interest, lump sum & annuity out of Accumulated Pension Corpus are paid **as admissible on exit BEFORE superannuation** *(Premature Exit: min **80% annuity** + max **20% lump sum**; if corpus **≤ ₹5 Lakh** [revised by PFRDA Dec 2025 from ₹2.5L], **100% lump sum** allowed)*.
- **1st Proviso [90-Day Waiting Period]:** Payment of lump sum and annuity **SHALL NOT BE MADE before expiry of 90 DAYS** from the date on which resignation becomes effective and Subscriber is relieved of duty!
- **2nd Proviso [Death within 90 Days]:** If Subscriber **dies before expiry of 90 days** from effective date of resignation, payment shall be made to the eligible person **IMMEDIATELY** (as per pre-superannuation exit norms)!
- **3rd Proviso [Non-Govt Continuation Option]:** Subscriber may, at his option, **continue to subscribe to NPS with the SAME PRAN as a non-Government subscriber**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Why the 90-day waiting period in 1st Proviso? Because 90 days is the outer limit for permitting withdrawal of resignation under Rule 14(3)(d)! Note also: under CCS (Payment of Gratuity under NPS) Rules, NO gratuity is payable on non-technical resignation!
cards.exam_trap: Why the 90-day waiting period in 1st Proviso? Because 90 days is the outer limit for permitting withdrawal of resignation under Rule 14(3)(d)! Note also: under CCS (Payment of Gratuity under NPS) Rules, NO gratuity is payable on non-technical resignation!

cards.front: [Rule 14(2) & 1st & 2nd Provisos | Proviso] What happens on 'Technical Resignation' (submitted with proper permission to take up another Central/State Govt appointment) under Rule 14(2) and its TWO Provisos?
cards.back:
- **Case 1 — New Central/State Dept IS covered by NPS [Rule 14(2) Main]:**
  - Subscriber **SHALL continue** to subscribe to NPS with the **SAME PRAN** on the new appointment (whether temporary or permanent), AND
  - **Shall be deemed to be a member of NPS from the date he joined Government service on the post to which he was FIRST appointed**!
- **Case 2 — New Central/State Dept is NOT covered by NPS [1st & 2nd Provisos to Rule 14(2)]:**
  - **1st Proviso:** Eligible to receive NPS exit benefits **AS ADMISSIBLE ON SUPERANNUATION (60% lump sum / 40% annuity)** *(NOT premature 20:80 exit!)*; **OR**
  - **2nd Proviso:** May, at his option, **continue to subscribe with the SAME PRAN as a non-Government subscriber**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Contrast Ordinary Resignation [Rule 14(1)] vs Technical Resignation to non-NPS Govt Dept [1st Proviso to Rule 14(2)]: Ordinary Resignation = 20:80 premature exit after 90 days; Technical Resignation to non-NPS Govt Dept = 60:40 SUPERANNUATION exit!
cards.exam_trap: Contrast Ordinary Resignation [Rule 14(1)] vs Technical Resignation to non-NPS Govt Dept [1st Proviso to Rule 14(2)]: Ordinary Resignation = 20:80 premature exit after 90 days; Technical Resignation to non-NPS Govt Dept = 60:40 SUPERANNUATION exit!

cards.front: [Rule 14(3)(a) to (e) | Sub-rule / Clause] List ALL FIVE mandatory statutory conditions under clauses (a) to (e) of Rule 14(3) under which the Appointing Authority may permit a person to withdraw his resignation in the public interest.
cards.exam_trap: Look closely at TWO traps in Rule 14(3): (1) Clause (a) BARS temporary Government servants from withdrawing accepted resignation under this rule; (2) Clause (d) measures 90 days up to the date ALLOWED TO RESUME DUTY (not merely date of application — unless relaxed under Rule 28 with MoPPGP concurrence)!

cards.front: [Rule 14(4) & Rule 14(5) | Exception] When MUST a request for withdrawal of resignation be REJECTED under Rule 14(4), and what is the automatic legal effect of an order allowing withdrawal of resignation under Rule 14(5)?
cards.back:
- **Mandatory Rejection [Rule 14(4)]:** Request for withdrawal of resignation **SHALL NOT BE ACCEPTED** by the Appointing Authority where a Government servant resigns with a view to taking up an appointment in or under:
  1. A **private commercial company**, OR
  2. A **Corporation or Company** wholly or substantially owned/controlled by the Government *(PSU)*, OR
  3. A **Body** controlled or financed by the Government *(Autonomous Body)*.
- **Deemed Condonation [Rule 14(5)]:** When an order is passed by the Appointing Authority allowing withdrawal of resignation and resumption of duty, **the order SHALL BE DEEMED TO INCLUDE THE CONDONATION OF INTERRUPTION IN SERVICE**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Resigning to join a PSU or Autonomous Body (just like a private company!) disqualifies the employee from withdrawing resignation under Rule 14(4).
cards.exam_trap: Resigning to join a PSU or Autonomous Body (just like a private company!) disqualifies the employee from withdrawing resignation under Rule 14(4).

cards.front: [Rule 15(1) + 1st & 2nd Provisos | Proviso] Explain the NPS rules on permitted absorption in a PSU / Autonomous or Statutory Body under Rule 15(1) and its TWO Provisos.
cards.back:
- **Deemed Retirement [Rule 15(1) Main]:** Permitted absorption in/under a Corporation/Company wholly/substantially owned/controlled by Central/State Govt, or a Body (autonomous or statutory) controlled/financed by Central/State Govt → **deemed to have retired from service from the date of such absorption** and eligible for **NPS SUPERANNUATION exit benefits (60:40)**.
- **1st Proviso [NPS Exists in New Body — MANDATORY Continuation]:** If NPS exists in the new organisation, the Subscriber **SHALL continue to subscribe with the SAME PRAN** in the new organisation, **SHALL NOT receive any NPS benefit at the time of absorption**, and shall receive benefits only after exit from the new body!
- **2nd Proviso [NPS Does NOT Exist in New Body]:** Subscriber may either draw superannuation exit benefits [15(1)] **OR opt to continue with the SAME PRAN as a non-Government subscriber**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Notice 'SHALL' in 1st Proviso to Rule 15(1) (reiterated in DoPPW OM dt. 07.10.2024): If the PSU/AB has NPS, the employee CANNOT cash out 60:40 at absorption — he MUST port the same PRAN!
cards.exam_trap: Notice 'SHALL' in 1st Proviso to Rule 15(1) (reiterated in DoPPW OM dt. 07.10.2024): If the PSU/AB has NPS, the employee CANNOT cash out 60:40 at absorption — he MUST port the same PRAN!

cards.front: [Rule 15(2), 15(3) & Explanations (1) & (2) | Sub-rule / Clause] Does Rule 15 cover Dept-to-PSU conversions and Joint Sector Undertakings [Rule 15(2)–(3)]? And what is the exact statutory 'Date of Absorption' in all 3 cases under Explanation (1)?
cards.back:
- **Rule 15(2) [Conversion of Govt Dept]:** Rule 15(1) applies on **conversion of a Central Govt Department** into a PSU or Autonomous Body controlled/financed by Central Govt.
- **Rule 15(3) [Joint Sector Undertakings]:** Rule 15(1) applies on permitted absorption in Joint Sector Undertakings **wholly under joint control** of (a) Central Govt + State Govt(s)/UT(s), OR (b) **two or more State Govts / UT Administrations**.
- **Explanation (1) — Exact 'Date of Absorption':**
  - **(i) Immediate absorption basis:** Date on which he **actually joins** that corporation/company/body;
  - **(ii) Initially joined on Foreign Service terms:** Date from which his **unqualified resignation is accepted** by the Government;
  - **(iii) Conversion of Govt Dept into PSU/AB:** Date from which his **option to be absorbed is accepted** by the Government.
- **Explanation (2):** *'Body'* means **autonomous body or statutory body**.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Match-the-following favourite: Immediate absorption = date of actual joining; Deputation/Foreign Service followed by absorption = date unqualified resignation accepted by Govt; Dept conversion = date absorption option accepted by Govt!

(a) Can PAO/CRA release his 20% lump sum on 15.05.2026? (b) What if 'K' tragically dies in a road accident on 15.05.2026?
cards.back:
- **(a) If 'K' is alive on 15.05.2026:** **NO!** Under **1st Proviso to Rule 14(1)**, lump sum and annuity **SHALL NOT BE PAID before expiry of 90 DAYS** from the effective date of resignation & relief (must wait until after 30.06.2026).
- **(b) If 'K' dies on 15.05.2026 (within the 90-day window):** Under **2nd Proviso to Rule 14(1)**, the 90-day bar is **lifted** — payment shall be made to the eligible person **IMMEDIATELY** *(as admissible in case of exit before superannuation)*! *(Note: OPS Family Pension under Rule 20 does NOT apply because 'K' had already resigned and ceased to be in service before death!)*

cards.front: [Rule 14(3)(a) & 14(4) — Case Study | Exception] [Case Study — Rule 14(3) & 14(4)] Can withdrawal of accepted resignation within 45 days be permitted by the Appointing Authority if: (Case A) Employee was a Temporary Govt servant? (Case B) Permanent employee resigned to join ONGC (a Central PSU), didn't like the job, and wants to return?
cards.back:
- **Case A (Temporary Govt Servant):** **NO!** **Rule 14(3)(a)** requires that *'the person concerned was **not a temporary Government servant** at the time of acceptance of his resignation'*.
- **Case B (Resigned to join ONGC / PSU):** **NO!** **Rule 14(4)** imposes a mandatory bar: withdrawal of resignation **shall NOT be accepted** where an employee resigns to take up appointment in a **private commercial company**, **Govt-owned/controlled Corporation/Company (PSU)**, or **Govt-controlled/financed Body (AB)**!

What two options does 'Z' have under the 1st and 2nd Provisos to Rule 14(2)?

2. **Option 2 [2nd Proviso to Rule 14(2)]:** Opt to **continue to subscribe to NPS with the SAME PRAN as a non-Government subscriber**.

**01.07.2026!**

cards.front: [Rule 16(1), 16(2) & Provisos | Proviso] How does Section 20 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 protect a disabled Subscriber under Rule 16(1)–(2), and who may apply for invalidation if the Subscriber himself is incapacitated?
cards.back:
- **RPwD Act Protection [Rule 16(1) + Proviso]:** Where **Section 20 of RPwD Act, 2016 (49 of 2016)** applies *(non-discrimination in Govt employment — no dispensation/reduction in rank on acquiring disability during service; shift to suitable post or keep on supernumerary post)*, the case is governed by Section 20 on producing a disability certificate under **RPwD Rules, 2017**.
- **Mandatory Counselling [2nd Proviso to Rule 16(2)]:** Even if a Subscriber covered by Sec. 20 RPwD Act applies to retire on invalidation, he **SHALL FIRST BE ADVISED** that he has the **option of continuing in service with the same pay matrix and service benefits**! Request is processed ONLY if he **does not withdraw** his retirement request.
- **Who Applies & Proxy Application [Rule 16(2) + 1st Proviso]:** Subscriber applies to **Head of Department (HOD)**. **1st Proviso:** Application submitted by **SPOUSE, failing which by a MEMBER OF THE FAMILY**, may also be accepted if HOD is satisfied Subscriber is unable to apply due to bodily/mental infirmity.

cards.front: [Rule 16(3)(a)–(b), 16(4), 16(5), 16(6), 16(7) & 16(8) | Timeline / Deadline] State the exact timelines, ₹54,000 pay threshold for Medical Authorities, Lady Doctor rule, Form number, and lower-post rule for medical examination under Rule 16(3)–(8)!
cards.back:
- **Timelines [Rule 16(3)]:** HOO/HOD requests medical authority **within 15 days** of receiving application, for examination **within 30 days** of receipt of request (supplying official age statement & endorsing copy to Subscriber).
- **Competent Medical Authority [Rule 16(3)(a)–(b)]:**
  - **(a) Medical Board:** For **ALL Gazetted** Government servants, AND **Non-Gazetted** Government servants whose pay [under FR 9(21)] **EXCEEDS ₹54,000 per mensem**!
  - **(b) Civil Surgeon / District Medical Officer / equivalent MO:** In all other cases *(Non-Gazetted with pay ≤ ₹54,000 p.m.)*.
- **Rule 16(4) [Duty to Appear & Two-Fold Medical Test]:** Subscriber **shall appear** before the concerned medical authority on the **date fixed by that authority**; medical authority examines him to ascertain **(i)** whether or not he is **fit for further service**, OR **(ii)** whether he is **fit for further service of less laborious character** than that which he had been doing.
- **Rule 16(5):** **No medical certificate** of incapacity may be granted unless requested by HOO/HOD.
- **Rule 16(6):** A **LADY DOCTOR shall be included** as a member of the Medical Board when a **woman candidate** is examined.
- **Rule 16(7):** Medical Certificate is issued in **Form 3**.
- **Rule 16(8):** If fit for **less laborious service**, employ on **lower post** (if willing); if no means of employing even on lower post → grant invalidation benefits.

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Triple exam bullseye: (1) Non-Gazetted Medical Board cut-off = pay EXCEEDING ₹54,000 p.m. (if exactly ₹54,000, Civil Surgeon/DMO suffices!); (2) Timelines = 15 days + 30 days; (3) Form = Form 3!

cards.front: [Rule 18(1) + Proviso & Rule 18(2) | Exception] If an NPS Subscriber is DISMISSED, REMOVED, or COMPULSORILY RETIRED AS A PENALTY under Rule 18, is his NPS Accumulated Pension Corpus forfeited like pension under CCS (Pension) Rules?
cards.back:
**NO! Accumulated Pension Corpus under NPS is NEVER forfeited under Rule 18!**
- **Rule 18(1):** Where a Subscriber is **compulsorily retired as a penalty**, **dismissed**, or **removed** from Government service, lump sum and annuity out of his Accumulated Pension Corpus **SHALL BE PAID to him** as admissible on **exit BEFORE superannuation** *(Premature Exit: max **20% lump sum** + min **80% annuity**; or 100% if corpus ≤ ₹5 Lakh)*.
- **Proviso to Rule 18(1):** Subscriber may, at his option, **continue to subscribe with the same PRAN as a non-Government subscriber**.
- **Rule 18(2) [Crucial Caveat for Gratuity!]:** Sub-rule (1) is **without prejudice** to action in respect of **Gratuity and other retirement benefits** not covered by these rules *(i.e., Gratuity IS forfeited on dismissal/removal [subject to compassionate gratuity] or reduced on compulsory retirement penalty under CCS Payment of Gratuity under NPS Rules, 2021)*!

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: One of the MOST tested contrasts in SAS / UPSC LDCE exams: Dismissal/Removal forfeits Pension & Gratuity under OPS (and forfeits Gratuity + UPS assured payout under UPS Rules 2025!), but under CCS (NPS) Rule 18(1), the NPS corpus (including 14% Govt contributions already credited!) is NOT forfeited — it only suffers Premature Exit (20:80)!

cards.front: [Rule 19(1) & Rule 19(2) | Exception] Can a retiring Subscriber's NPS Accumulated Pension Corpus (60% lump sum or 40% annuity) be withheld due to Departmental or Judicial Proceedings pending on retirement under Rule 19?
cards.back:
**NO! Pending proceedings CANNOT block or reduce NPS Corpus payout!**
- **Rule 19(1):** Departmental or judicial proceedings instituted while in service (not concluded before retirement), OR judicial proceedings instituted after retirement:
  - **SHALL NOT AFFECT** the benefits payable out of his Accumulated Pension Corpus, AND
  - Lump sum and annuity **SHALL BE PAID** as admissible on **exit ON SUPERANNUATION (60% lump sum + 40% annuity)**!
- **Rule 19(2) [Gratuity Caveat]:** Without prejudice to action in respect of **Gratuity and other retirement benefits** *(under CCS Payment of Gratuity under NPS Rules, 2021 & DoPPW OM dt. 27.10.2022, **Gratuity** SHALL be withheld during pending departmental/judicial proceedings and may be recovered/withheld for grave misconduct or pecuniary loss)*.

cards.front: [Rule 20(1)(a)–(b) + Proviso, 20(2) & 20(3) | Proviso] Explain ALL provisions of Rule 20 on Death of a Subscriber (including death of a retired Invalid/Disability Pensioner under clause (b)), the EOP Proviso, and who receives the Employee's NPS share under Rule 20(2)!
cards.back:
- **Who Gets OPS Family Pension [Rule 20(1)(a)–(b)]:** On death of:
  - **(a)** A serving Subscriber whose exercised/default option under Rule 10 is for OPS/EOP; **OR**
  - **(b)** A **retired Subscriber who was in receipt of Invalid Pension (Rule 16) or Disability Pension (Rule 17)**,

- **PROVISO to Rule 20(1):** If death is **attributable to Government service**, HOO disburses benefits under **CCS (Extraordinary Pension) Rules, 1939 [now 2023]** (subject to fulfilling EOP conditions).
- **Settlement of NPS Corpus when OPS/EOP Family Pension Paid [Rule 20(2)]:**
  1. **Government contribution + returns thereon** → transferred to **Government Account**.
  2. **Remaining corpus (Employee contribution + returns)** → paid in **LUMP SUM** to the **person(s) nominated under PFRDA (Exits & Withdrawals) Regulations, 2015**; if **no nomination subsists** → paid to **LEGAL HEIR(S)**!

cards.front: [Rule 16(4), 16(7) & 16(8) | Sub-rule / Clause] What happens under Rule 16(8) if the Medical Authority certifies in Form 3 that the Subscriber is 'fit for further service of less laborious character', EXCEPT the Subscriber is NOT willing to accept a lower post?
cards.back:
Read **Rule 16(8)** word-for-word: *'If the Subscriber, has been found to be fit for further service of less laborious character than that which he had been doing, he shall, **PROVIDED HE IS WILLING TO BE SO EMPLOYED**, be employed on lower post and **if there be no means of employing him even on a lower post**, he may be granted benefits on retirement on invalidation.'*

- Employment on a lower post requires the Subscriber's **willingness**.
- Invalidation retirement benefits under Rule 16(8) are granted when **there is no means of employing him even on a lower post** *(subject always to RPwD Act Sec. 20 protection of pay/rank where applicable under Rule 16(1))!*

2. **2nd Proviso to Rule 16(2):** If such Subscriber nevertheless applies to retire under Rule 16, he **MUST be formally advised** of his right to continue in service with the **same pay matrix and service benefits**; his invalidation request can be processed **only if he does not withdraw** his request after being so advised.

cards.front: [Rules 16(11) & 17(3) + Rule 22 of CCS (Gratuity under NPS) Rules, 2021 & OM dt. 28.10.2022 | Exception] CRITICAL CROSS-RULE EXCEPTION: When an NPS Subscriber with ONLY 3 years of service is discharged on Invalidation [Rule 16] or Disablement [Rule 17] (opting for NPS corpus benefits), does he get Retirement Gratuity (which needs 5 years) or DEATH GRATUITY rates?
cards.back:
**He gets Gratuity at DEATH GRATUITY RATES (NO 5-year minimum qualifying service barrier!)**
- Explicitly clarified in **Para 15 of DoPPW O.M. No. 57/03/2022-P&PW(B)/8361(1) dated 28.10.2022** read with **Rule 22 of CCS (Payment of Gratuity under NPS) Rules, 2021**:
- Where a Central Govt servant covered under NPS is discharged from service on **invalidation [Rule 16]** or **disablement [Rule 17]**, in addition to his NPS corpus / OPS pension entitlement, gratuity is payable **at DEATH GRATUITY slab rates** (`<1 yr = 2×`; `1 to <5 yrs = 6×`; `5 to <11 yrs = 12×`; `11 to <20 yrs = 20×`; `≥20 yrs = ½ emoluments per 6-monthly period up to 33×`, subject to **₹25 Lakh** cap)!
- Hence with 3 years' service (`1 to <5 yrs` slab), he receives **6 times monthly emoluments** as gratuity!

cards.front: [Rule 17 & Rule 20(1) Proviso + CCS (Extraordinary Pension) Rules, 2023 [G.S.R. 63(E)] | 2024–2026 Update] When an NPS Subscriber's Rule 10 option/default is for EOP on service-attributable Disablement [Rule 17] or Death [Rule 20(1) Proviso], how do Categories A, B, C, D & E of the CCS (Extraordinary Pension) Rules, 2023 operate?
cards.back:
Notified vide **G.S.R. 63(E) dated 30.01.2023** (explicitly incorporating **Rule 10 of CCS NPS Rules, 2021** in its Application Proviso):
- **Category A:** Death/disability **NOT attributable to nor aggravated by** Govt service *(governed by ordinary CCS Pension Rules Invalid/Family Pension under Rules 16 / 20(1)(a), NOT EOP)*.
- **Category B:** Death/disability **attributable to OR aggravated by** Govt service *(e.g., occupational disease / duty accident)* → EOP Family Pension (`60%` of basic pay) / Disability Pension (`service element + disability element for 100% disability = 30%`, proportionate down to 20%).
- **Category C:** Accidents while performing **strictly official duty** (e.g., official travel/air/rail/sea mishap, natural calamities on duty).
- **Category D:** Acts of violence by **terrorists, anti-social elements, extremists, border skirmishes, sea piracy** → Liberalised Family/Disability Pension (`80%` family pension!).
- **Category E:** Operations specially notified by Govt, **war / war-like operations, enemy action, evacuation of Indian nationals abroad** → Highest Liberalised Award (**`100%` of last pay** as Liberalised Family Pension!) + **Constant Attendant Allowance** where 100% disabled!

⚠️ EXAM TRAP / PROVISO ALERT: Remember: Whenever EOP benefits under Categories B/C/D/E are disbursed via Rule 17(1) or Rule 20(1) Proviso, **Rule 17(2) / Rule 20(2)** still returns **100% of Employee's own NPS contribution + returns** in lump sum while transferring only Govt share + returns to Govt Account!

cards.front: [Rule 21(1), (2), (3) & (4) | Timeline / Deadline] Detail the quarterly retirement list calendar, responsible authority, look-ahead window, PAO submission dates, and non-superannuation intimations under Rule 21(1)–(4).
cards.back:
- **Quarterly Preparation by HOD [Rule 21(1)]:** Every **Head of Department (HOD)** shall prepare a list **every 3 months** — on **1st January, 1st April, 1st July, and 1st October** each year — of all Subscribers due to retire **within the next 12 to 15 months** from that date.
- **Supply to PAO [Rule 21(2)]:** Copy supplied to **PAO** not later than **31st January, 30th April, 31st July, or 31st October** respectively.
- **Retirement Other Than Superannuation [Rule 21(3)]:** **Head of Office (HOO)** shall **promptly inform DDO and PAO** as soon as the fact of such retirement becomes known.
- **Endorsement to Directorate of Estates [Rule 21(4)]:** If the Subscriber under Rule 21(3) is an **allottee of Government accommodation**, HOO shall endorse a copy of the intimation to the **Directorate of Estates**.
